### Observed differences

- **Early segment rewired.** In the earlier window, A40 handed control to A14 (about 38 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions), A15 (about 31) or A20 (about 32), and each of these three always passed control on to A21. In the later window, A40 leads directly to A21 in every observed case, and A14, A15 and A20 instead lead to A23 (about 39–54 in 100) or straight to A27 (about 46–61 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, LAG004]

- **Later segment rewired.** In the earlier window, A22 always passed to A23 and A23 always to A27. In the later window, A22 passes to A23 in about 52 of 100 cases and to one of A14/A15/A20 in about 48, while A23 passes to A27 in about 48 of 100 cases and to one of A14/A15/A20 in about 52. [DIR004, DIR005]

- **Order relations flipped.** In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 always executed before A21 and before A22 whenever they co-occurred (for example, A14 before A21 in 38 of 100 traces). In the later window they execute after A21 and A22 (for example, A21 before A14 in about 31 of 100). Relative to A23 the order is now mixed, with both directions observed. [REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL003, REL008]

- **Positions shifted.** A14, A15 and A20 moved from roughly a third of the way through the trace (mean positions about 0.31–0.33) to about 60% through (about 0.59–0.60), while A21, A22 and A23 each moved slightly earlier (about 0.02–0.03). The share of traces containing each of the three activities stayed similar, about 30–38 in 100 in both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

- **Step distances changed accordingly.** A22 to A23, previously always one step apart, is now two steps apart in about half the cases; A23 to A27 likewise (about half at two steps); A22 to A27 moved from two to three steps; A40 to A21 moved from two steps to one. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the group of alternative activities A14, A15 and A20 was relocated from the segment between A40 and A21 to the later segment between A22 and A27: in the earlier window one of the three ran directly after A40 and handed control to A21, whereas in the later window A40 leads straight to A21 and the group executes in the A22–A27 segment — before A23 in about half of the traces and after A23 in the other half — before control reaches A27. [DIR006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

The supporting signs are direct and consistent: the successor changes are observed at every involved activity; the order relations with A21 and A22 flip completely between the windows; the group's position shifts from about a third to about 60% of the trace while its participation stays stable (about 30–38 in 100 traces in both windows), so the activities were neither added nor dropped; and 24 control-flow items qualified against fewer than 1 expected without change, far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [DIR006, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a single relocation from removing the group at the early position and re-inserting it later, and the reading that the group executes exactly once between A22 and A27 rests on the lag distributions rather than on a direct count of repetitions per trace. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Other differences: none beyond the above; the slight forward shifts of A21, A22 and A23 accompany the same relocation [POS004, POS005, POS006].
